Back to Blog Highnote Teams Up with Visa to Launch Agentic Commerce Capabilities

Modern card platform Highnote unveiled its new Agentic Commerce capabilities this week.

Built using Visa Intelligent Commerce, Highnote’s Agentic Commerce will allow businesses to power AI-initiated payments that feature programmable controls, tokenized credentials, and dynamic authorization.

Headquartered in San Francisco, Highnote made its Finovate debut at FinovateSpring 2022. Courtesy of a partnership with Visa, Highnote—a modern issuing, acquiring, credit, ledger, and money movement platform—has launched its new Agentic Commerce capabilities this week. Built using Visa Intelligent Commerce, the new offering will enable businesses to securely power AI-initiated payments with programmable controls, tokenized credentials, and dynamic authorization. The new Agentic Commerce capabilities will allow companies to add payment capabilities to AI agents while enabling software to initiate and execute transactions with predefined rules, spend controls, and approval structures. In a statement announcing the launch, Highnote listed invoice and accounts payable automation, vendor payments, operational spend management, and AI-assisted procurement as some of the initial use cases for the new solution. “AI is quickly moving from insight to action,” Highnote CEO John MacIlwaine said. “Businesses want AI to do more than recommend or analyze. They want it to initiate and execute real financial workflows. The challenge is making those transactions secure, controlled, and operational at scale. That’s exactly what Highnote is built to do.” Agentic commerce enables software to participate directly in purchasing and payment decisions based on preset authorization rules. The new capabilities give firms a structured framework for enabling AI-driven transactions with real-time visibility and decisioning across the payment lifecycle. Highnote’s Agentic Commerce offering will also support emerging financial operations powered by AI, such as intelligent procurement, dynamic payment routing, supplier optimization, recurring operational spend, and industry-specific autonomous payment experiences. “Agentic commerce is already changing how businesses operate,” said Visa VP and Head of Agentic CMS Ivy Lee. “Through Visa Intelligent Commerce, we’re enabling B2B workflows where agents can initiate and complete transactions at scale. Visa provides the underlying infrastructure that makes this possible—handling the complexity so businesses and developers can focus on building differentiated experiences, not payments.” Headquartered in San Francisco, California, Highnote made its Finovate debut at FinovateSpring 2022. At the conference, the company demonstrated how its modern card platform with a GraphQL-based API enables businesses to make card issuance an embedded capability. The demo also featured the developer experience and financial operations interface that provides control of the payment transaction lifecycle and access to transaction processing data. Named to the Forbes Fintech 50 for a second consecutive year, Highnote last month unveiled expanded commercial card issuing capabilities for online travel agencies (OTAs), marketplaces, and travel platforms. The new offering enables these platforms to run on Highnote’s commercial card issuing platform, using virtual card programs that are purpose-built for the challenges of travel supplier payments. Highnote’s solution combines issuing, controls, ledger, and reconciliation into a single system in order to deliver faster reconciliation, bolster supplier relationships, and improve unit economics on every transaction. data.title: Highnote Powers a New Era of Commercial Card Issuing for Online Travel
data.ai_summary: Highnote announced expanded commercial card issuing capabilities for online travel agencies (OTAs), marketplaces, and travel platforms, providing infrastructure for virtual card programs purpose-built for travel supplier payments at scale. The platform enables single-use virtual cards tied to bookings, staged supplier capture, granular spend controls, and an integrated ledger with real-time visibility, allowing customers to launch programs in weeks rather than quarters. Both major global card networks have publicly highlighted Highnote's role in modern travel payments in their recent earnings calls.
data.author: Business Wire

industries.name: Virtual Card Issuance & Tokenized Corporate Cards

data.full_text:
OTA platforms can now run on Highnote’s commercial card issuing platform, with virtual card programs purpose-built for travel supplier payments at scale SAN FRANCISCO–(BUSINESS WIRE)–Highnote, the unified platform for modern issuing, acquiring, credit, ledger, and money movement, today announced expanded commercial card issuing capabilities for online travel agencies (OTAs), marketplaces, and travel platforms. Leading OTA platforms now operate virtual card programs on Highnote, with purpose-built workflows for the unique demands of travel supplier payments.

Highnote’s commercial card issuing platform gives travel companies the infrastructure to build differentiated supplier payment programs at scale. Customers can configure single-use virtual cards tied to bookings, staged supplier capture, and granular spend controls across merchant categories, all underpinned by an integrated ledger that delivers real-time visibility into every authorization and capture. The result is faster reconciliation, stronger supplier relationships, and improved unit economics on every transaction, driven in part by access to wholesale travel BINs across both major global card networks. Both major card networks have publicly highlighted Highnote’s role in modern travel payments in their most recent earnings calls. “Travel is one of the most demanding environments in commercial payments, and what our customers are building on Highnote reflects that,” said John MacIlwaine, CEO of Highnote. “Our platform was purpose-built so that the leading OTAs and travel marketplaces can move faster, differentiate their payment experiences, and continuously innovate while operating at scale. We are proud to power their programs, and we are seeing this same model unlock better economics across many other industries as well.” Unlike fragmented legacy approaches that require travel platforms to stitch together multiple vendors and inconsistent economics, Highnote brings issuing, controls, ledger, and reconciliation into a single system. This allows customers to launch programs in weeks rather than quarters and to evolve them continuously as their business grows. Highnote has also further optimized its Virtual Card Express (VCX) solution, which enables companies to launch and scale virtual card programs with speed and efficiency, by incorporating access to these wholesale travel BINs. This allows platforms to onboard faster and streamline the implementation of modern supplier payment models. These capabilities are available today as part of Highnote’s commercial card issuing programs and are delivered in partnership with Highnote’s onboarding, compliance, and program management teams. To learn more about Highnote’s commercial card issuing platform for travel, visit https://highnote.com/solutions/travel.
